title: General adic finite-reduction pullback interface
statement:
Let $g:T'\to T$ be a morphism of schemes and let $A,I,P_n=A/I^n$, $S_{W,n}=(P_n)_W$, and $B_W=A_W$ for $W=T,T'$ be the general Noetherian adic coefficient datum of [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum]. Write $\pi_{W,n}:B_W\to S_{W,n}$ for its projection and $q_{W,b,a}:S_{W,b}\to S_{W,a}$ for its quotient maps. Use the strict reduction $\mathcal R_T$ and canonical universal tower pullback $\widetilde L_0$ of [def-weil-pbc-completed-pullback], with the finite coefficient identifications of [lem-weil-pbc-constant-completion-equivalence]. The finite-reduction interface consists of the following fixed constructions, for all $n\geq1$ and $b\geq a\geq1$, without a completeness or boundedness condition on $K\in D(\operatorname{Mod}(B_T))$.

The ordinary finite pullback is $g_n^*$ on $S_{T,n}$-modules with its tensor-formula coefficient map; this is $\operatorname{completedReductionFiniteModules}$. The finite target functor $B_n(K)=Lg_n^*(K\otimes^L_{B_T}S_{T,n})$ is $\operatorname{completedReductionFiniteTarget}$. The canonical finite evaluation isomorphism $F_{0,n}:\operatorname{ev}'_n\widetilde L_0\mathcal R_T\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Res}_{\pi_{T',n}}B_n$ is $\operatorname{completedReductionFiniteEvaluation}$, defined by the unique comparison whose K-flat representative equation uses the universal strict-tower counits and the ordinary comparison normalized on local inverse-image tensor generators.

For a $B_T$-module sheaf $M$, $V\in T_{\mathrm{pro\acute et}}$, $U\in T'_{\mathrm{pro\acute et}}$, an arrow $f:U\to g^*V$, and sections $s\in S_{T',n}(U)$, $z\in S_{T,n}(V)$, $m\in M(V)$, the section $s\otimes g^{-1}_f(z\otimes m)$ in $g_n^*(M\otimes_{B_T}S_{T,n})(U)$, formed with the inverse-image adjunction unit and sheafified scalar tensors, is $\operatorname{completedReductionFiniteGenerator}$. For a cochain complex $P$ of $B_T$-modules, the canonical computation arrow from $B_n(QP)$ to $Q(g_n^*(P\otimes_{B_T}S_{T,n}))$, formed from the scalar-extension complex counit followed by exact finite pullback localization, is $\operatorname{completedReductionFiniteModelMap}$.

The ordinary quotient transition from $g_b^*(M\otimes_{B_T}S_{T,b})$ to $\operatorname{Res}_{q_{T',b,a}}g_a^*(M\otimes_{B_T}S_{T,a})$ is the unique natural map sending the generator indexed by $(s,z,m)$ to that indexed by $(q_{T',b,a}(s),q_{T,b,a}(z),m)$; it is $\operatorname{completedReductionOrdinaryTransition}$. Its unique descent characterized on K-flat representatives via the preceding computation arrows and the canonical restriction localization is $\operatorname{completedReductionTargetTransition}:B_b\to\operatorname{Res}_{q_{T',b,a}}B_a$. Its scalar-extension adjoint $B_b(K)\otimes^L_{S_{T',b}}S_{T',a}\to B_a(K)$ is $\operatorname{completedReductionTargetNormalization}$.

For $c\geq b\geq a$ and $N\in D(\operatorname{Mod}(S_{W,c}))$, the canonical scalar associativity comparison $(N\otimes^L_{S_{W,c}}S_{W,b})\otimes^L_{S_{W,b}}S_{W,a}\xrightarrow{\sim}N\otimes^L_{S_{W,c}}S_{W,a}$, using the actual quotient composition identity and the standard scalar adjunctions, is $\operatorname{completedReductionQuotientAssoc}$. At equal indices the scalar-extension counit composed with the extension of the inverse of the sectionwise-identity restriction comparison is $\operatorname{completedReductionUnit}$. These names denote the existing canonical constructions, not independently chosen maps; their transition coherence is a separate assertion. Natural index $i$ in Lean represents the positive exponent $i+1$.
